name: sentineltx-mcp

tools.name: lookup_address
tools.description:
Look up a blockchain address. Returns labels, risk tags, entity info, balance.
Works for Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, BSC, and 100+ chains.
For deep fund-flow tracing or report generation, use start_investigation instead.

address.description: Blockchain address (0x..., T..., bc1..., r..., etc.)

tools.name: validate_address
tools.description: Validate a blockchain address format and detect which chain it belongs to. Use this before any tracing tool to confirm the address parses cleanly.

tools.name: start_investigation
tools.description:
Start a blockchain forensic investigation. Returns a session_id immediately.

Use for: multi-hop fund tracing, cross-chain bridge detection, suspect-to-exchange
flow analysis, AML / STR report generation, victim-fund recovery analysis.

Typical investigations take 2–10 minutes. After calling this, tell the user the
estimated time and then call check_investigation(session_id) once or twice with
some natural delay to retrieve the result.

mode.description: 'investigation' (default) for forensic / law-enforcement use; 'compliance' for AML / STR reporting on a deposit address

headless.description: Default true. When true, the trace runs server-side — no SentinelTX dashboard needed. Set false only if a human user is going to open the SentinelTX dashboard in a browser to watch it run.

tools.name: check_investigation
tools.description:
Check the status of an investigation started by start_investigation.

Long-polls server-side up to ~45s; returns early on status change.
Returns one of:
- status="queued"   — accepted, agent about to start.
- status="running"  — in progress; call again.
- status="complete" — full assistant_text is ready.
- status="error"    — investigation failed.

Typical pattern: call check_investigation 2–4 times. Each call blocks
server-side for up to 45 seconds (or returns early on status change).

wait_sec.description: Server-side long-poll budget. Default 45. Set 0 for an instant snapshot.

tools.name: cancel_investigation
tools.description:
Cancel a running investigation started by start_investigation.

Use this when the user wants to abort early — wrong address, taking too long, etc.
The session status flips to "cancelled". Idempotent: cancelling an already-terminal
session is a no-op. Only the session owner can cancel.

tools.name: get_investigation_graph
tools.description:
Export the fund-flow graph (nodes + links) of a completed investigation.

Returns a share URL that any HTTP client can GET to receive the graph JSON.
The 24h token in the URL is the credential — no login required for that URL.

Set include_payload=true to inline the graph JSON in the tool result —
convenient for small graphs but uses more model context.

Graph shape:
- nodes[]: { id (address), label, group, depth, balance, amount_in,
  amount_out, tx_count, risk_score?, tags?[], ... }
- links[]: { source (address), target (address), value, token?, count,
  direction, hop }

session_id.description: session_id returned from start_investigation. Investigation must be in 'complete' state.

include_payload.description: Inline the full graph JSON in this tool result. Default false.
